title: Walkers in Rust: a baked navmesh, one nav update a tick, bodies moved by the desired velocity
note: Register game.navigation with the walker's config, bake in on_reset, call sim.nav.update once a tick, move each body by its desired velocity, then set_position.
intent: Walkers path on genex's nav, never a hand-made grid. Register game.navigation(NavConfig::walker(radius, height)) once; when a character controller moves the bodies, register character.nav_config() instead, so every path is one the capsule can climb. In on_reset build NavInput::new() from the level (.with_static_colliders(&sim.physics, NavArea::WALK) with physics, else .with_triangles or .with_terrain), NavMesh::bake it and sim.nav.add_mesh; a big level registers game.nav_bake(name, ..) and loads the bytes with NavMesh::from_bytes_for. Each tick: sim.nav.update(ctx.dt) once, then per agent read nav.desired_velocity, move the body (the character's drive; CharacterMotion::Mixed for root motion) and report nav.set_position(agent, feet, velocity). nav.status says no-path, off-mesh or target-off-mesh when a target or an agent is off the walkable mesh, and at-link when the agent waits for the game to play a crossing (nav.take_link, then nav.finish_link). Probe sim.nav.probe(); for a capture draw frame.nav_debug(&sim.nav, NavDebug::mesh().with_paths()).
port: One facet registers game.navigation and owns the bake and the update; a facet that adds walkers adds agents to sim.nav and moves only its own bodies.

evidence.note: The walker config, NavInput and NavMesh::bake in on_reset, sim.nav.update once a tick, desired_velocity then set_position, the statuses, links, offline bakes, the probe and NavDebug.
character.nav_config() matches the bake to the capsule's climb and slope.
Moving things: game.navigation(..) for walkers and paths.
